title: Phased microbenchmarking framework for sequence-length aware kernel ranking
creator: Miguel Alvarez
description: Background: Our current kernel-picking layer relies on static heuristics + a small online probe for new models. As token distributions get bimodal (short chat turns vs long-context retrieval), the static ranking produces suboptimal choices for mixed workloads, causing tail latency regressions under certain seq-length mixes. Goal: build a phased microbenchmarking and ranking framework that produces a stable, sequence-length-bucketed kernel ordering per architecture (GPU SKU + driver) and per model family, with controlled exploration during rollout and a safe fallback path.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Per-arch, per-model-family kernel ranking produced from microbenchmarks across predefined seq-len buckets (e.g., 8, 64, 256, 1024) available in the runtime metadata store. 2) Online selector uses ranking + lightweight bandit exploration and fails back to the highest-confidence kernel without violating latency SLO in >=99% of requests. 3) Telemetry shows decreased p99 latency or cost-per-token compared to baseline for at least 3 production workloads during canary. 4) Rollout docs and runbook exist.
design_notes: - Phase 0: offline microbenchmark harness that runs short probe jobs across kernels, seq-len buckets, batch sizes and records p50/p95/p99, warmup stability, GPU occupancy and memory headroom. - Phase 1: fingerprinting: capture hardware (arch, driver), model hash, typical seq-len histogram and infer nearest neighbor historical profiles. - Phase 2: ranking: combine microbench results with a small cost model (tokens/sec + tail factor) and produce a score per kernel per bucket. Use a robust aggregator (median-of-bootstraps) to avoid noisy microbench samples. - Phase 3: rollout: enable bandit-lite exploration for low volume traffic, ramp up with automatic rollback if p99 regresses > 10% or error rate increases. - Instrumentation: add per-request kernel_choice, kernel_version, seq_len_bucket labels to traces/metrics. - Safety: implement hard SLO guard that can preempt exploration and switch to pinned fallback kernel.
implementation_todo: - Extend microbench harness (runtime/bench) to include prefills and decode loops; add configurable seq-len and batch sweeps. - Add results ingestion pipeline: bench results -> ingestion lambda -> runtime metadata store. - Implement ranking service that scores kernels and exposes an API /v1/kernel-ranking?model=<>&arch=<>. - Selector update: selector consults ranking API, uses contextual fingerprinting to pick candidate kernel, then bandit policy decides whether to probe alternatives. - Telemetry: add dashboards for per-kernel p50/p95/p99, cost-per-1M-tokens, and exploration rate.
tradeoffs_and_notes: - Microbench cost vs coverage: more buckets increase accuracy but cost more GPU time; we will start with 4 buckets and expand if customer workloads show long-tail gaps. - Bandit exploration adds noise to production metrics; use conservative epsilon-decay and only probe <1% of traffic initially. - Should we use GP/ML model to predict kernel performance across seq-len/arch? MVP will use nearest-neighbor interpolation + linear cost model; leave GP for follow-up if we need better interpolation.
qa_and_testing: - Local unit tests for harness config parsing. - CI job that runs microbench smoke on our smallest test GPU. - Staging canary: run ranking on staging models, route 0.5% traffic for 48h, compare telemetry. - Run a controlled A/B test against a synthetic mixed seq-length load generator and measure p99 and tokens/sec.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dev cluster: run bench, validate ingestion and ranking API. 2) Staging canary with selected internal models (1 day). 3) Production canary 0.5% traffic for 72h, monitor p99 and error rate. 4) Gradual ramp to 5% then 25% if stable. 5) Full rollout. Rollback: automated if p99 > baseline * 1.10 for 30m.

2025-02-18 Infra review (Riley Chen): Suggested using time-series store for per-bench samples and a compact aggregated row for ranking API to minimize lookups.
2025-02-21 Data (Sofia Nguyen): Proposed nearest-neighbor interpolation using model-family + arch fingerprint; deferred GP model to follow-up due to engineering cost.
2025-02-25 Priya Raman: Bench harness PR opened (see links). Running initial microbench on dev-gpu-1; early results show surprising kernel A advantage at bucket 64 but worse at 1024.

2025-03-01 Performance (Evan Brooks): Observed p99 spikes during exploration in staging when exploration rate was 2%. Reduced to 0.5% and spikes disappeared. Note: need better warmup for kernels with large JIT costs.
